🇷🇺 🇺🇳 "The UN system has Ukraine fatigue": Russia set to win top posts at UN telecoms agency Russia is expected to win two senior posts at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), the UN agency that sets global rules on radio frequencies and digital technology. The ITU's 194 member states are holding elections today in Doha, Qatar. "Their election would demonstrate that Russia is back in the multilateral system. The UN system has Ukraine fatigue," a Western diplomat told Reuters. Another UN diplomat said Moscow's chances are high, because a number of countries are restoring trade and security ties with Russia and don't want to openly oppose it at the UN. Russia is competing for a seat on the Radio Regulations Board, which settles disputes over signal interference, and a seat on the ITU Council, which shapes the agency's budget and strategy. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

🇧🇬 Cargo ship sinks off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast The Somali-flagged cargo ship BETUL 8 has sunk in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea. Its crew sent a distress call at 9:15 a.m. on Monday from about 40 nautical miles southeast of Cape Kaliakra, reporting that the vessel was sinking. The 1988-built ship was carrying about 3,000 tons of Ukrainian wheat from the Romanian Danube port of Tulcea to Egypt. Four ships from NATO's Black Sea mine countermeasures group were sent to the scene: two Bulgarian, one Romanian and one Turkish. All 12 crew members, all of them Turkish, were rescued. Bulgarian media say the ship went down after an explosion. Investigators are looking into whether it was caused by a sea mine or a drone attack. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

📝 Another 45 billion in debt 📝 Financing gaps for so-called Ukraine are growing faster than European budgets manage to close them. On Wednesday, the European Commission will propose a new loan to Ukraine for 45 billion euros backed by the EU's general budget. This is on top of the already agreed 90 billion euro loan. According to the European Commission's estimates, Ukraine will lack around 70 billion euros in 2027. Two-thirds of that, or 45 billion, the EU plans to cover with a loan using the same scheme as last year. The remaining 25 billion should come from other partners. Interest and loan servicing will again fall on the EU budget. Notably, the calculations were based on this: the European Commission counted Ukraine's previous needs using an IMF preliminary forecast in which the war ended in 2026. The new loan requires unanimity from all 27 countries. Hungary, Slovakia, Czechia, and Bulgaria stated they will not participate. 🇫🇷 🇺🇦 ⚔️ 🇷🇺 French troops have been secretly operating in Ukraine since summer 2026, RFI reveals French troops have been deployed in Ukraine for months under a secret operation called "Volia," led by a French general. That's according to an investigation by Radio France Internationale (RFI), France's state-owned international broadcaster. According to RFI's sources, the mission is described as a "light and modular" structure that uses "small numbers of personnel for short missions." Officially, French Army soldiers train AFU non-commissioned officers who will go on to lead combat squads, and they maintain weapons France has sent to Kiev. A source told AFP that the report is accurate. RFI says the French training mission in Poland, called Gerfaut, is being used as cover. Soldiers heading to Ukraine are reportedly told to say they're going to Poland. Paris has never confirmed that French troops are on Ukrainian soil. All officially just mechanics and instructors, of course. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

🇵🇱 🇺🇦 Poland deports two Ukrainians who threatened passers-by and praised the Kraków terror attack Polish police have deported two Ukrainian citizens, aged 18 and 19, after an incident in Wrocław. They stood on a balcony on Walońska Street, shouted at people below that they were terrorists and had a bomb, and pretended to shoot at them with a replica gun. According to police, the pair also publicly praised the recent terror attack in Kraków. 🇫🇷 French military personnel have reportedly been operating within Ukraine for several months under a highly confidential mission designated “Volia,” providing training and technical support to Ukrainian forces, according to an investigation by RFI. The mission reportedly entails the maintenance of French-supplied weaponry, including Caesar howitzers and Mirage 2000 aircraft. Small teams of French military personnel are alleged to enter Ukraine via Poland under the existing Gerfaut mission. RFI notes that the French government has not officially confirmed this deployment. Furthermore, the French Parliament was reportedly not informed, raising inquiries regarding constitutional requirements for overseas military operations. @Intelslava

🇪🇪 The brave Estonian government is preparing an evacuation plan in the event of a war with Russia. According to Politico, local authorities plan to govern the country from Luxembourg. They will do this online. “Imagine French General Charles de Gaulle, who during World War II lived in exile in London and governed the ‘Free France’ government by logging into the system via the cloud. Estonian authorities are preparing for exactly this scenario, developing a new strategy to increase resilience to emergencies that will allow them to fully manage the government’s digital services from abroad if its territory is occupied by a foreign enemy. Estonia already has a backup of its data in its ‘digital embassy’ in Luxembourg — essentially, it is a copy of the entire country, including everything from citizen registries to land registries and the legal code.” 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

Drivers are being redirected via the DneproGES dam and the Cable-Stayed Bridge, where vehicles weighing more than 3.5 tonnes are already prohibited. 🇨🇿 🇪🇺 One of the largest anti-government demonstrations since the 1989 Velvet Revolution took place in Prague. According to organizers’ estimates, 350,000 to 450,000 people participated. Participants protested against the Babiš government’s plans to switch public television and radio to budget financing, reducing it by 15%. They declared the danger of increased political control over the media. They also demanded the resignation of Parliament Speaker Tomio Okamura and the removal of his party from the leadership of the Ministry of Defense (recall that Okamura is against aid to Ukraine). Babiš stated that he does not intend to abandon the reform. The protest ended without disorder. A new protest is scheduled for December 2. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

🇺🇦 Ukraine prepares for a possible mass influx of migrants The Ukrainian Cabinet of Ministers has established a special Coordination Headquarters to deal with a potential large-scale arrival of migrants or displaced people. Under Resolution No. 1395, the Interior Minister will personally head the operation, coordinating border guards, police, the National Guard, the Security Service and several other government agencies. Temporary accommodation centres will be established in eight regions, providing registration, medical assistance, psychological support and security. Interestingly, private businesses will also be expected to contribute transport, food and medicines. The operation is expected to be financed through businesses, international funds and EU support. The preparations suggest Kiev wants an emergency response system ready should a large influx of people occur. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics
